journey:kazimirowski-divine-mercy.t: Divine Mercy (Jesus, I Trust in You)

x.summary: This is the first image of the Divine Mercy, painted under the direction of the Polish nun Saint Faustina Kowalska, who described a vision of Christ she had received in 1931. Christ steps forward in a white robe, one hand raised in blessing and the other touching his heart, from which pale and red rays stream out. Faustina was disappointed that no painting could equal what she had seen, but this canvas became the source of one of the most widespread Catholic devotions of the modern age.
facts: Faustina and her confessor, Blessed Michał Sopoćko, regularly visited Kazimirowski's studio to guide the work, and Sopoćko himself posed for the figure of Christ.
According to Faustina's diary, the pale ray stands for water and the red ray for blood, the 'blood and water' that flowed from Christ's side.

After the Soviets closed St Michael's Church in 1948, the painting was hidden, taken to a parish in Belarus and in 1986 secretly brought back to Vilnius; since 2005 it has hung above the main altar of the Divine Mercy Sanctuary.
